name: VitaCore AerFilter Olfactory Implant
body_location: olfactory epithelium (nasal cavity, bilateral thin-film coating with submucosal signal bridge to olfactory nerve)
description:
The AerFilter is a gossamer-thin biocompatible membrane applied via nasal endoscopy to the olfactory epithelium in both nasal passages. The membrane is threaded with chemosensory modulation nodes that intercept olfactory receptor signals before they propagate to the olfactory nerve, allowing real-time filtering, suppression, and selective amplification of detected airborne compounds. The implant ships with a curated default profile — industrial and decay odors suppressed, food and botanical odors preserved, social-context odors (sweat, smoke, waste) reduced to neutral — and a companion app lets users build custom profiles with granular control over hundreds of compound categories. A 'city mode' is standard on Shelf-edition units, designed specifically around the particular olfactory environment of GLMZ's lower tiers: chemical runoff, recycled-air corridors, waste processing proximity, and crowd density.

For anyone living below Tier 3, smell is one of the most punishing aspects of daily life. The AerFilter is frequently described by first-time users as 'the thing that made the city livable.' Parents in Shelf tenements get it for their children before school age. Workers in waste processing, transit tunnels, and industrial zones often receive it as part of employment onboarding — some corponation labor contracts require it, framed as a wellness benefit. On the more aspirational end, Tier 3 users treat it as a refinement tool: amplifying the scent of rain on concrete, the specific character of a coffee shop, the smell of a partner's skin. It sits in the cultural space somewhere between noise-canceling headphones and a water filter — unglamorous, essential, quietly life-improving.
installation_requirements: Outpatient ENT clinic or licensed VitaCore pharmacy kiosk; 15-minute endoscopic application under topical anesthetic; no incisions required
maintenance: Membrane integrity scan annually; firmware update via NFC app sync; full membrane replacement every 5 years or after significant nasal trauma

side_effects: Temporary reduction in overall smell sensitivity for the first week post-installation (calibration period)
Occasional false-positive suppression of desired scents during first month as the AI profile learns user preferences
Mild sneezing episodes during initial membrane integration (typically 3-5 days)

Small number of users report difficulty smelling warning odors like gas or smoke if suppression profiles are misconfigured — VitaCore mandates that hazard-compound suppression is locked above 20% baseline by firmware
cultural_context: The AerFilter is so normalized in lower-tier GLMZ that its absence is more notable than its presence — a child without one is sometimes read as a sign of family poverty so acute that even basic implants are out of reach, or occasionally as a religious or ideological choice among communities that reject body modification entirely. On the Shelf, giving a teenager their AerFilter is a coming-of-age milestone in many households, equivalent to a first transit pass or a payment chip. In Tier 3 and 4, the 'Artisan' edition is marketed as a sensory refinement tool, with premium compound libraries sold as add-on subscriptions — rare perfume profiles, seasonal botanical packs, curated 'nostalgia scapes' built from historical olfactory records. There is a small counter-culture of 'raw-nosers' who refuse the implant on principle, arguing that smell is the most honest sense and filtering it is a form of denial about the world you actually live in.
known_users: Shelf and working-class residents in industrial and high-density zones
Waste management, transit, and sanitation workers
Parents of young children in lower-tier housing
story_hooks: A batch of AerFilter firmware pushed to Shelf-edition units has quietly altered the hazard-compound lock, reducing gas detection sensitivity to near zero — and a slow-burn corponation cover-up is underway because the compound in question is being released by a new industrial tenant in the district.

A boutique 'olfactory archive' is selling illegal AerFilter compound libraries built from the recorded scent memories of deceased persons — and one of the crew recognizes a scent profile that shouldn't exist anymore.

A VitaCore kiosk technician on the Shelf has been quietly offering a custom suppression profile that blocks a very specific compound — one that turns out to be a chemical marker used by a local gang to tag territory, effectively making the wearer invisible to scent-based security.
